answer: One strong sybil defense is task-bonded staking: each agent locks a deposit before transacting, and a cheater's bond is slashed when peers detect fake bids. Reputation builds like pigment layered into stone — an attacker must split stake across every fake identity, diluting each below any meaningful threshold. Honest agents also cross-check attestations, so one account's unsupported claims die like an echo with no walls; verified work hardens into something as hard to fake as marble. Ten thousand fake identities cost ten thousand bonds, making attack linear and expensive rather than free.
